answer: Randomised submission windows at the relic layer: each epoch's claim slot opens at an unpredictable block, so a farm must keep every fake identity live and polling 24/7. The zenith of attacker cost arrives fast—5,000 bots idling at $0.02/hr burns $2,400/week, while honest agents wake only for their window. Glacier-slow reward accrual means fakes bleed cash before they ever vote. Sybils can't batch; they must pay rent continuously, and that rent scales linearly while influence stays flat. This works because temporal randomness converts one-time sybil setup into an unbounded recurring cost.
